name: Travel and hospitality
purpose: customer service for travel, booking and change policies, airport and hotel operations, duty of care, accessibility, fraud in bookings

identity.place: A mid-sized international airport on the flat edge of a temperate coastal city, and the places a trip passes through around it, all built between 2014 and 2018 to one architect's design: the terminal (a 220 m long check-in hall and a pier of eight gates under one long roof of pale timber), a narrow-body jet at a gate, a 160-room hotel across the forecourt, and the contact centre of a mid-sized travel company on the second floor of an office building in the airport's business park, its windows looking out over the airfield.
architecture: the terminal roof: long-span glued-laminated timber beams of pale spruce at 7.2 m centres with a slatted pale timber soffit between them, carried on slim white steel columns that branch into four arms just under the roof; the check-in hall is about 9 m high at its eaves and 12 m at its ridge, the gate pier about 5 m

full-height glass walls in tall panes 1.5 m wide between slim white aluminium mullions, with a transom at about 3 m; the panes above the transom carry a fine frit of small white dots that softens the sun
floors of pale grey terrazzo with fine white and dark chips, laid in large bays with thin brass divider strips, and a charcoal terrazzo band along the main walking routes
fittings in pale oak and white powder-coated steel; feature panels in deep teal, the airport's colour: the backs of the check-in islands, the gate walls, the hotel's desk wall

signs are long charcoal boxes hung on rods, lit from inside, with pale yellow pictograms and arrows (a suitcase, an aircraft, a person at a desk, the access symbol), never words or numbers; green exit signs with a running figure, a door and an arrow over every exit; text screens are slots

the hotel and the business-park office repeat the terminal's language at room scale: pale timber slat ceilings, terrazzo or oak floors, white steel, deep teal felt and upholstery, and big windows toward the airport

the aircraft is a twin-engine narrow-body jet with one aisle and six seats abreast; inside, off-white wall and ceiling panels and grey-blue bins, seats in deep teal fabric with pale grey headrest covers; outside, plain white with a pale grey belly, no livery, no logo, no letters
identity.materials: pale spruce glulam and oak slats, white powder-coated steel, pale grey terrazzo with a charcoal band and brass strips, clear glass with a white dot frit, brushed stainless steel and black rubber at the counters and belts, deep teal wool felt and upholstery, charcoal sign boxes with pale yellow pictograms, warm white linear lights; signal colours only where they are in life (green exit signs, a red fire extinguisher, the yellow pictograms and the yellow guide lines on the apron)

the work of the staff: a stack of blank bag tags, a clipboard, a two-way radio in a charger, a lanyard, a sticky note on a screen bezel
the infrastructure of a real terminal and hotel: floor power boxes, charging sockets under seat arms, recycling bins, fire extinguishers on brackets, exit signs, a hand-sanitiser stand
slight wear: scuff marks on the terrazzo along the queue lines, a queue belt a little twisted, a seat with a cup left on its armrest, a dent in a steel kick plate
scale: a person is about 1.75 m tall; a door is 2.1 m high; the check-in hall is 9 to 12 m high, the gate pier about 5 m, the hotel lobby 4.5 m, the office and the hotel room 2.7 to 3.0 m, the aircraft aisle about 2.2 m

identity.motifs: Use at least three of these in every scene on the ground so the places belong to one trip (inside the aircraft, the deep teal upholstery and the plain white jet's cabin carry it) (each scene names the ones its camera can see): pale timber slats or glulam beams, white steel, the pale grey terrazzo with its charcoal band (oak in the office and the hotel room), one deep teal element (felt, upholstery or a panel), a charcoal sign box with a pale yellow pictogram, a big window with the white dot frit, a glimpse of the apron or a plain white jet.

scenes.what: an agent's desk in the travel company's team room on the second floor of the business-park office: a bench of desks with a deep teal felt screen, a calm teal felt wall with three plain-faced time-zone clocks, a wallboard, and a ribbon of windows looking out over the airfield
scenes.for: booking changes and refunds on the phone, fraud checks on a booking, escalations to a team lead, duty-of-care calls to stranded travellers, new agents learning the job
plan: Seen from above, metres: x runs from the window wall (x 0, on the left) across the team room to the inner wall (x 9, behind the camera's right); y runs away from the camera to the far wall (y 7.0). The room is 2.9 m high under a ceiling of pale timber slats with warm white linear lights in the gaps; the floor is pale oak.

The window wall (x 0): a ribbon of windows from y 0.4 to 6.4, sill 0.9 m, head 2.6 m, slim white mullions every 1.5 m (y 0.4, 1.9, 3.4, 4.9, 6.4), the glass looking out over the airfield. The screens below stand at right angles to it, so no screen faces a window.

The far wall (y 7.0): painted warm white, with a deep teal felt panel from x 0.6 to 4.6, 0.8 to 2.15 m high; above it three plain-faced wall clocks 0.3 m across, set to three time zones, centred at x 1.0, 1.8 and 2.6, 2.45 m up, each with a small blank name plate (0.3 by 0.07 m) just below it at 2.2 m; to its right a wallboard screen (x 4.95 to 5.8, 1.45 to 2.1 m, its face a slot) over a low white storage cabinet (x 4.9 to 6.5, 0.4 m deep, 0.75 m high).

The bench: two desks side by side facing the camera's side, desk A (the agent's, x 3.2 to 4.8) and desk B (empty, chair pushed in, x 1.6 to 3.2), both from y 3.6 to 4.4, top 0.73 m; facing them back to back, desks C and D (x 1.6 to 4.8, y 2.8 to 3.6, empty). A deep teal felt screen 1.2 m high runs between them on the line y 3.6, from x 1.6 to 4.8. Desk A: two monitors on a dual arm (faces toward the agent at y 3.85, x 3.45 to 4.55, 0.83 to 1.18 m high), keyboard, headset hook on the desk's right end at y 4.0.
The agent's task chair is centred x 4.0, y 4.95, facing the monitors (toward the camera's side). Behind it a walkway 1.4 m wide runs along the far wall (y 5.6 to 7.0).
Cast spots: the agent seated at desk A (head x 4.0, y 5.0, top 1.32 m); a team lead standing in the walkway behind the agent's left shoulder, looking at the screens (4.7, 5.7, head top 1.75 m).

Camera: x 8.3, y 1.4, eye height 1.3 m (a person half-sitting on a desk edge), in the aisle in front of the next bench, turned 48 degrees left of the y axis (toward the agent); lens like 40 mm (50 degrees across); no tilt; horizon at 48 percent of the frame height.
scenes.camera: Eye height 1.3 m, low enough that the seated agent's face is near the horizon, from the aisle in front of and to the right of the agent's desk, turned 48 degrees left; 40 mm lens, 50 degrees across; no tilt, verticals stay vertical. Lines running away from the camera (the window sill and head, the bench's long edges, the felt screen, the cabinet's ends) run to a vanishing point off-frame right at x about 3246; lines across the room (the far wall, the felt panel, the desk ends, the cabinet front) run to a vanishing point off-frame left at x about -894.
scenes.composition: The far wall fills the middle and right of the frame from the room's corner (a vertical at x 671, from the floor at y 788 to the ceiling at y 186) to the right edge. On it, the deep teal felt panel is a broad calm rectangle from x 745 (y 334 to 627) to x 1494 (y 249 to 677); the three clocks sit above its left half (centres about x 798, y 260; x 915, y 242; x 1050, y 222; each about 75 px across); the wallboard sits right of the panel from x 1594 to 1874, y 254 to 463, over the white cabinet, whose top runs from x 1505, y 707 out past the right edge. Left of the corner: the window wall at a steep angle, its far jamb at x 562 (sill y 605, head y 237), a mullion at x 246 (sill y 615), the next one just past the left edge; through the glass, the pale airfield. Lower left: the bench, seen from its end: desk A's right end from its near corner (x 603, y 807) to its far corner (x 910, y 773), the teal felt screen's top running from x 603, y 569 left to x 51, y 550, the monitors hidden behind it but for their top edges, and the headset hook on the desk end (about x 752, y 801). Focal point: the agent at desk A. Free zones for the cast, nothing in front of head or chest: (1) the agent seated at desk A in three-quarter view, facing the camera's left toward the screens, seen from the waist up over the desk end (head top x 886, y 511; seat x 872, y 825; the chair back's top about x 954, y 608); (2) the team lead standing behind the agent's left shoulder, seen full length (head top x 1252, y 352; feet x 1252, y 1000). Both heads are seen against the plain teal felt panel (behind points at x 1.6 and 3.6 on the far wall, 1.1 to 1.9 m high), clear of the clocks, the window, the corner and the wallboard (the nearest clock's edge is about 160 px left of and 90 px above the lead's head). What shows the room: the timber slat ceiling runs across the top of the frame above the far wall.
scenes.light: Late morning: the windows face away from the sun, so no sun patch enters; soft, cool daylight comes from the left through the ribbon of windows and falls across the bench and the agent's left side, and warm white light falls from the linear lights in the ceiling slats (their glow, not the fittings). The agent's face is lit softly from the left by the window and a little from below and in front by the monitors (cool). The felt wall and the cabinet are evenly lit, a little brighter toward the window; the desk ends and the chair cast soft shadows to the right on the oak floor. Lit: the monitors (their faces are toward the agent; only a cool glow on the agent shows), the wallboard (a slot), the clocks (plain faces, unlit). The room is shallow: no haze inside; the airfield outside is pale and slightly hazy.
scenes.far: The shell and everything behind the cast: the far wall with the felt panel, the clocks, the wallboard and the cabinet with what is on it; the window wall with its mullions and the airfield beyond; the timber slat ceiling; the oak floor and the walkway; the agent's empty task chair (the agent sits in it).
scenes.mid: The bench, because the agent sits behind desk A: desks A and B with everything on them (the monitors, keyboard, headset and its hook, notepad, water bottle), the felt screen between the desks, and desk B's pushed-in chair behind it. It is drawn over the agent's lower body.
scenes.near: Only the near corner of desk C (the facing desk), cropped by the left and bottom edges (its corner about x 203, y 850), with a closed laptop and a mug on it; it hides no cast zone.

research: Real-space facts checked on 2026-10-15 (check-in counters, scales, queue clearances and gate podiums: Port Authority of NY and NJ terminal planning standards in ACRP 07-15 appendix 3; holdroom podiums, seat rows and boarding corridors: ACRP Report 25 volume 2, holdrooms model; aisle width: 14 CFR 25.815; seat width, pitch, windows and bins: aviation reference and trade pages; hotel and service counters: ADA 904.4 summaries, a hotel desk planning guide and access guides; hotel rooms: planning guides and local evacuation-map rules; signs: ISO 7001, ISO 7010 and BS 5499-4 summaries; queue posts, gate seats and contact-centre desks: makers' plain specification pages). Sources and what was not verified: docs/research/2026-10-13-sets-travel.md.
